doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

chapter: Harry James, Damone and Los Angeles
title: Proving himself in the L.A. studios
summary: He took the L.A. TV work to test himself against top studio players and names his section mates on Hollywood Palace and the Tom Jones Show.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: was playing bass. Jack Sperling was playing drums, I forget who the saxophone player was. Did that. And the reason I moved to L.A., Vic Damone — I had a lot of exposure with Vic Damone. They wrote a couple of charts where I had a chance to play — be featured like. And the conductor for “Hollywood Palace” happened to be in town and came to that show and he heard me play and he asked me if I’d like to come down and be lead trumpet player at “Hollywood Palace.” And I talked to Vic and I told Vic about it and Vic says, “Well how much are you making?” And I told him. He said, “I’ll give you more.” So he made me an offer I couldn’t refuse. So I stayed another year. The following year I got sounded again to go down and do it and I did it. And the reason I really did that is I wanted to put a check on myself. Am I good enough to be a top studio player? You know, when the heat’s on. Am I good enough to play as well as those guys? And I did that and I went down and I found out that I was. That satisfied my feeling about how my playing was. Because I had never played with that caliber player — we had good caliber players here but they’re top notch guys down there. John Audino and all those guys.
Yeah I was going to ask who you were sitting next to in those days?

Well at the “Hollywood Palace” it was pretty impressive, I’ll tell ya. “Hollywood Palace” was Manny Klein, Ray Triscari, Sweets Edison and myself. That was one show. And we did the “Tom Jones Show” that was Audino, Ray Triscari, Jimmy Zito and myself. And at both of those shows every time something would come in with some Gs or stuff like that, Manny Klein would go, “Pass that to the kid.” So I used to get all of that because they didn’t want to play it so they’d pass it to me. And then I say like the small band, just Conte Candoli and myself.
